- Overestimate prices when sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.3) — model tends to overshoot early in positive sentiment cycles.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.4) — model fails to capture downward momentum or panic.
- Model consistently overreacts to recent spikes — forecast peaks too early and too high, especially after sentiment turns positive.
- Mean reversion bias: model often holds prices too high after a spike, ignoring recent downward sentiment or technical correction.
- Horizon-specific: 30-day forecasts are overly optimistic in early 2024/2025, especially when sentiment is volatile or mixed — model doesn’t adjust for sentiment volatility.
- Lagged sentiment effect: if sentiment turns negative within 5–7 days, model still holds high prices — should adjust downward by 1–2 days ahead.
- Avoid “sentiment echo” — model mirrors sentiment too closely, especially when sentiment is low, leading to underestimation of downside risk.
- When sentiment is neutral or mildly positive, model tends to overproject upward trend — reduce forecast slope if sentiment < 0.1.
